title: bug: foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:861 reds the whole daemon leg once src reaches 592 test files
description:
Filed by worker-319873d7 from task-bd2f1ecf186f4ab5884c2a3ada07108e (Gate 3 release authorization). NOT a defect in that row's diff — measured, see the control below. Out of that row's owned paths, so filed rather than fixed inline.

SYMPTOM. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (which is `vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=30000 src`) exits 1 with exactly one failure:
  src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:861:24  expect(outcome.ok).toBe(true)  -> received false
  Test Files 1 failed | 591 passed (592). Tests 1 failed | 10571 passed | 8 skipped (10580).
Reproduced twice, back to back (733.80s and 414.69s runs). Not a random flake.

MEASUREMENT, four runs, all foreground on the same host and tree:
1. src (592 files), maxWorkers=4 -> EXIT 1, the failure above.
2. src (592 files), maxWorkers=4, repeat -> EXIT 1, identical failure.
3. The failing file ALONE, `--testTimeout=30000` passed explicitly (the package script's flag is dropped when you narrow) -> EXIT 0, Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 8 passed (8), 171.40s.
4a. src with `--exclude "**/release-decide-authorization.test.ts"` (591 files) -> EXIT 0, 591 passed (591), 10553 passed | 8 skipped.
4b. THE CONTROL: src with `--exclude "**/release-decide-wiring.test.ts"` (591 files), the new authorization file KEPT and its 19 arms executing (10566 passed vs 10553) -> EXIT 0, 591 passed (591).

4b is the decisive one. Removing a DIFFERENT file clears the red just as well as removing the new one, so the trigger is the suite reaching 592 files under maxWorkers=4, not any particular file's content. The new authorization file's own test time is 289ms, far too small to be load.

LIKELY CAUSE, from the failing arm's OWN comment at :836-842: it launches a REAL provider session child ("the produced argv is a real provider session rather than `--version`, so the child's latency is the provider's: observed at 100s and 122s on this host, which made the old 120_000 bound a coin flip. 240_000 keeps a real bound"). The bound was already documented as marginal. At 592 files under 4 workers the co-scheduling shifts enough that the launch exceeds it, and settlement never releases the worktree, so `outcome.ok` is false.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE ROW. The daemon leg is the owned-package gate for every row touching apps/daemon. As written it fails for the NEXT row that adds a test file, whoever that is, and the failure names a file that row never touched — so each one pays the same multi-run attribution cost this row just paid. The bound is a host-latency coin flip that the file count decides.

SUGGESTED DIRECTIONS (not a prescription): raise or remove the 240_000 provider bound on that arm; or make the arm's provider launch a fake on the parallel lane and keep the real one behind an opt-in; or pin the arm to its own worker/sequence so co-scheduling cannot move it. Whoever takes it should re-run the control above rather than trusting this record.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE: the release authorization change. Its own primary gate `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release` is EXIT 0, 13 files / 135 tests, and the failing file imports nothing that row touched (grep-verified per file: no reference to release-decide-command.ts, release-decide-service.ts or daemon-command-async-entries.ts).
definitionOfDone: Reproduce the red at 592 daemon test files under --maxWorkers=4, then re-run BOTH controls from the description (exclude the authorization file; exclude a different file) and confirm each returns 591 passed EXIT 0 — the file-count trigger must be re-measured, not assumed from this record.

Name the actual mechanism with evidence (child-process latency against the 240_000 bound, worker co-scheduling, or worktree settlement), quoting the measured launch duration rather than inferring it from the arm's comment.

Land a fix that makes `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 at the CURRENT file count AND at count+1: add one throwaway trivial test file, prove the leg still exits 0, then remove it. A fix that only greens today's count re-arms for the next row.

The arm keeps asserting what it asserts today: settlement released the worktree, the boundary was actually reached, and the launch was a real provider session on whichever lane still runs it. Weakening the assertion or deleting the arm is not a fix.
Record the fresh foreground count lines and exit codes for the daemon leg, and disclose any foreign red with path attribution rather than calling it green.
